title: Deformable Texture Maps: Compiling Dynamic Microgeometry into Neural Textures
abstract: Deformable material surfaces, such as cloth, owe their appearance to fine-scale geometries that restructure under deformation. Even when coarse simulation models efficiently recover this microstructure, explicitly instantiating and rendering it remains expensive. We introduce Deformable Texture Maps (DTM), a representation that compiles deformation-driven microgeometry into a continuous and compact neural texture. Our model maps texture coordinates and local deformations to intrinsic maps describing opacity, surface normals, depth, and material identity. This captures the occlusion and visibility changes generated by deformation. At runtime, these maps provide a common texture-space representation of deformation-driven fine-scale structure that can be evaluated directly on coarse deforming surfaces. Since our representation encodes geometric attributes rather than radiance, lighting and material response remain decoupled from the learned model. This allows us to apply relighting, as well as shading and material editing without retraining. We further introduce a persistent texture-space rendering strategy that caches these intrinsic maps and selectively updates them as deformation changes. This effectively decouples neural evaluation from frame rendering and enables their reuse across frames and conventional rendering effects. We demonstrate our approach on yarn-based textiles, where non-linear material stretch and shear induce changes in yarn geometry, spacing and occlusion. We build our model by, first, sweeping tileable yarn patches through deformation space, then, rendering the detailed geometry into a canonical texture-space, and finally, compressing the resulting maps into a single neural representation. Our resulting model can be evaluated directly on arbitrary coarse garment meshes and integrated with conventional shading pipelines, keeping appearance authorable at render time.

analysis.sourceNote: 依据 arXiv 2611.13677v1 精确版本全文及关键页面，PDF 共 12 页。实验数字均为作者报告。
analysis.ideaZh: DTM 将纱线微几何在不同拉伸和剪切下的变化编译成神经纹理。网络输出 opacity、normal、depth 和 material ID，粗布面可以直接着色、换色并复用缓存，适合需要近看仍有纱线细节的可编辑布料资产。
methodFlow: 对纱线 tile 采样拉伸与剪切
在共享 UV 域渲染四种属性图
在粗布面按需更新缓存并独立着色
analysis.whyRelevantZh: 适合借鉴其把可编辑颜色和形变条件分开保存的资产表示。
analysis.evidenceZh: 共享 UV 域让不同形变状态能使用同一个纹理坐标。（Fig. 2, §§3.1–3.2, PDF pp. 3–5） 运行时换色后，色块仍沿变形的纱线结构。（Fig. 9, §5.3, PDF p. 9） 作者报告，宽度 128 的 RIB 模型占 0.263 MiB，in-distribution 材料 ID 准确率 96.18%。（Table 3, §5.1, PDF p. 7）
analysis.caveatZh: 每种微结构独立训练，证据限于采样域内插值。表面属性图对强视差、深遮挡和透射的表达有限。 迁移到刺绣需要把纱线纹理条件换成针迹拓扑和受力模型，论文没有验证这一迁移。
analysis.motivationZh: 粗布面能模拟宏观褶皱，显式实例化每根纱线会让渲染、存储和实时编辑变得昂贵。
analysis.methodZh: 先在局部拉伸和剪切网格上生成微几何，将结果拉回统一的材料 UV 域并栅格化固有属性。Fourier-SIREN 以 UV 和形变量预测属性图，运行时按形变和 LOD 更新纹理缓存。
analysis.experimentsZh: 五种 woven/knitted 结构分别训练，覆盖离线重建、服装示例、重着色与运行时缓存。 作者报告，宽度 128 的 RIB 模型占 0.263 MiB，in-distribution 材料 ID 准确率 96.18%。（Table 3, §5.1, PDF p. 7） 比较 ASTC、原始属性图与邻近纹理线性混合。Table 3 的压缩结果基于 RIB。 §6 比较近似参数量的 MLP 架构和缓存设置。缓存收益随局部形变和视点变化而变。
analysis.insightZh: 把形变后的微几何属性保存在可直接着色的纹理域中，材料 ID 保留颜色编辑接口。
